{:db/id 17592186198361 :knowledge-point/canonical-example {:db/id 17592186198235 :question/id #uuid "9d477733-7178-5b88-926f-a457faaf344a" :question/math-academy-id "e-7285" :question/problem "Consider the region $D$ in the $xy$-plane, given by

$$
D = \big\{ (x,y) \: : \: -2 \leq 4x+2y \leq 2, \:\: 0 \leq y-x \leq 3 \big\}.
$$

By performing the change of variables $u = 4x+2y$ and $v=y - x,$ write the following integral in terms of $u$ and $v.$ 

$$
\displaystyle 
\iint\limits_D \sin \left(3(x+y)\right)  \: \mathrm{d}x \, \mathrm{d}y
$$" :question/worked-solution "Let's define a transformation $\mathbf{T}$ as follows:

$$
\mathbf{T}: {\left[ \begin{array}{c}u \\ v\end{array} \right]} 
\longrightarrow 
{\left[ \begin{array}{c}x ( u , v ) \\ y ( u , v )\end{array} \right]}
$$

This transformation maps some region $\Delta$ in the $uv$-plane to our region $D$ in the $xy$-plane.

To compute the required integral, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
\iint\limits_{D} f(x,y) \, \mathrm d x \, \mathrm d y = \iint\limits_{\Delta} \ f(x(u,v), y(u,v))  \left| \dfrac{\partial (x, y)}{\partial (u, v)} \right|  \mathrm d u \, \mathrm d v
$$

where $\dfrac{\partial (x, y)}{\partial (u, v)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $\mathbf{T}.$

Note that the change of variables

$$
u = 4x + 2y, \qquad v = y - x
$$

 

gives us the *inverse* function $\mathbf T^{-1},$ that is

$$
\mathbf{T}^{-1}:{\left[ \begin{array}{c}x \\ y\end{array} \right]} \to {\left[ \begin{array}{c}u ( x , y ) \\ v ( x , y )\end{array} \right]}.
$$

To compute the required integral, we proceed as follows:

**Step 1**: Find $\Delta,$ which is the image of $D$ under the action of $\mathbf{T}^{-1}.$ 

Our domain in the $uv$-plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ & =\{(u,v)\,:\,-2\le u\le 2,\,0\le v\le 3\}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $\mathbf T^{-1}.$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $\mathbf T^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\begin{vmatrix}4 & 2 \\ -1 & \text{ }\text{ }1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $\mathbf T.$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $\mathbf T$ is

$$
\dfrac{\partial (x, y)}{\partial (u, v)} = \left( \dfrac{\partial (u, v)}{\partial (x, y)} \right)^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{6}.
$$

Note that $\dfrac{\partial (x, y)}{\partial (u, v)} \neq 0$ everywhere inside $\Delta.$ In other words, $\mathbf T$ has no critical points inside $\Delta.$

**Step 4**: Perform the change of variables.

In this case, we first need to solve the transformation equations

$$
u = 4x+2y, \qquad v = y-x
$$

 
for $x$ and $y$, which gives

$$
x = \dfrac{u-2v}6, \qquad y =\dfrac{u+4v}6.
$$

 

Performing the change of variables, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3(x+y))\,dx\,dy & ={∬}_{Δ}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3(\frac{u-2v}{6}+\frac{u+4v}{6}))|\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|\text{d}u\,\text{d}v \\  & ={∬}_{Δ}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\left(\frac{2u+2v}{6}\right))|\frac{1}{6}|\text{d}u\,\text{d}v \\  & =\frac{1}{6}{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{-2}^{2}sin\,(u+v)\,du\,dv.\end{aligned}
$$"} :knowledge-point/id #uuid "9fed8ac2-8d21-5bc9-b1cc-df20760cfbfb" :knowledge-point/key-prerequisites [{:db/id 17592186050705 :topic/id #uuid "6047b0c9-9ae0-5fc8-9179-8ce5172d5c9d" :topic/knowledge-points [{:db/id 17592186129197} {:db/id 17592186129261} {:db/id 17592186129262}] :topic/math-academy-id 1998 :topic/next [{:db/id 17592186050482}] :topic/title "Computing Areas Using a Change of Variables"}] :knowledge-point/level-coverage [{:db/ident :question.difficulty/easy} {:db/ident :question.difficulty/moderate}] :knowledge-point/question-generator {:db/id 17592186539392 :question-generator/id #uuid "88a49b66-1e9c-5b35-8e4c-127a3b9a4c84" :question-generator/script "generate/scratch/17592186198361.py"} :knowledge-point/questions [{:db/id 17592186198948 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "994baf38-6869-57c8-804b-1e89962812d1" :answer/type {:db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "\frac{1}{2}\displaystyle \int_{0}^{3}\displaystyle \int_{0}^{2}uvdvdu" :db/id 17592186197559} {:answer/id #uuid "d214aef4-d04e-532d-9308-a674c66f4c11" :answer/type {:db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "\displaystyle \int_{0}^{3}\displaystyle \int_{0}^{2}(v^{2} - $$

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ & =\{(u,v)\,:\,1\le u\le 4,\,1\le v\le 10\}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\begin{vmatrix}y & x \\ 1 & 1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =y-x.\end{aligned}
$$

.

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}={\left(\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)}\right)}^{-1}=\frac{1}{y-x}
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

**Step 4**: Perform the change of variables, and evaluate the integral:

Performing the change of variables, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}|y-x|\,{e}^{xy}\,dxdy & ={∬}_{Δ}|y-x|\,{e}^{u}\,|\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v \\  & ={∬}_{Δ}|y-x|\,{e}^{u}\,\frac{1}{|y-x|}\,\text{d}u\text{d}v \\  & ={∬}_{Δ}{e}^{u}\,\text{d}u\text{d}v \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{4}[{\int }_{1}^{10}{e}^{u}\,dv]du \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{4}{e}^{u}[{\int }_{1}^{10}dv]du \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{4}{e}^{u}[v]_{1}^{10}\,du \\  & =9{\int }_{1}^{4}{e}^{u}\,du \\  & =9[{e}^{u}]_{1}^{4} \\  & =9({e}^{4}-e).\end{aligned}

u=\frac{y}{{x}^{2}},\,v=xy

gives us the *inverse* function ${\mathbf{T}}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{\mathbf{T}}^{-1}:\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}\to \begin{bmatrix}u(x,y) \\ v(x,y)\end{bmatrix}.
$$

To compute the required integral, we proceed as follows::

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $D$ under the action of ${\mathbf{T}}^{-1}.$ 

Our domain in the $uv$-plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathrm{Δ} & =\{(u,v)\hspace{0.167em}:\hspace{0.167em}1\le u\le 4,\hspace{1em}1\le v\le 5\}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${\mathbf{T}}^{-1}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\begin{vmatrix}-\frac{2y}{{x}^{3}} & \frac{1}{{x}^{2}} \\ y & \text{ }\text{ }x\end{vmatrix} \\  & =-\frac{3y}{{x}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}={\left(\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)}\right)}^{-1}=\frac{1}{\left(-\frac{3y}{{x}^{2}}\right)}=-\frac{1}{3u}.

$$
